target_customer: Public adjusters, restoration contents firms and insurers who build contents inventories for claims
problem: Contents inventories for insurance claims are typed in by hand line by line. InventoryQuant turns video or audio walkthroughs into priced line items and submission-ready inventories.
business_model: B2B SaaS for claims professionals, pricing not found

founders.name: Sander Schulhoff
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as an AI researcher who wrote an early prompt engineering guide and ran the first GenAI red-teaming competition. Education and employers not listed.

competitors.name: Adjusto
competitors.what: AI-native contents claims services and FairMatch valuation platform

competitors.name: claimtouch with Snapsheet
competitors.what: AI contents claims platform covering inventory, valuation and settlement

competitors.name: Enservio
competitors.what: Contents valuation platform including straight-through contents

technical_complexity.rationale: Video and audio understanding, item recognition and replacement pricing are now achievable with foundation models but accuracy and price matching are hard for one founder.

defensibility.rationale: Several funded contents-claims vendors exist and the workflow can be copied. Integrations such as XactContents export help but do not lock customers in.

market_need_then: The company says contents work is manual and costs thousands of man hours; one law firm testimonial on its site says it saved days, which is a vendor-chosen quote. 2025 launches by competitors show insurer demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses inventoryquant.com, an exact .com. A USPTO word mark was filed 2025-08-10 and registered 2026-03-10 by the founder.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, practical and plain-spoken for claims workers ('Made for the people who walk the loss site')

branding.brand_signature: Made for the people who walk the loss site

brand_strength.rationale: Clear and descriptive for the niche but generic with no independent press; the founder's own audience from Learn Prompting is a separate brand.

outcome_analysis: InventoryQuant is a one person Winter 2026 company building contents inventory automation for insurance claims. It has one named customer testimonial and no verified funding or revenue. The outcome is open, with the founder's AI credibility an asset and the crowded contents-claims field and solo staffing the main risks.
notes: Unverified funding: Crunchbase shows a pre-seed from Y Combinator with hidden amounts and Dealroom shows a $125K seed, both aggregators, so no round is recorded. Learn Prompting funding claims (a Series A banner on Caplight) were not tied to the company and were ignored. Dealroom lists New York City HQ while YC says San Francisco. Completeness pass: the 125K seed rests on a single database (Dealroom) with no date or investors. Crunchbase lists a pre-seed from Y Combinator with hidden amount. No press coverage found.
